# 🛡️ dsh-permission-rules - **1024 store channel**: `npm i -g dsh1024` once, then `dsh1024 plugin --profile web add dsh-permission-rules` (counts toward the [deepseek1024.com](https://deepseek1024.com) install ranking). [![Gitee](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gitee-mirror-c71d23?logo=gitee)](https://gitee.com/perrylink/dsh-permission-rules) [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?metric=downloads)](https://dshfind.com/plugins/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?ref=badge) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/badge)](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules) **Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness.** *Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not.* [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--plugin-✅-green)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) [![dsh-doctor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor/main/badges/PerryLink__dsh-permission-rules.svg)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-plugin-doctor#verified-徽章) [![DSH Market](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/2BingLing/dsh-market/master/assets/readme/badge-top-rated.svg)](https://dsh.market/) [![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-brightgreen.svg)](#) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/ci.yml?branch=main&label=CI)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/actions) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/github/v/tag/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules?label=version)](https://github.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/releases) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-permission-rules)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-permission-rules) [English](README.md) · [简体中文](README-zh.md) · [Español](README-es.md) · [Português](README-pt.md) · [हिन्दी](README-hi.md)
--- **📖 Ecosystem knowledge base** — measured data, not marketing: [plugin development guide · plugin-selection data · maintenance criteria](https://perrylink.github.io/dsh-plugin-guide/). ## ⭐ 如果它帮到了你 这个插件是 [DSH 插件家族](https://github.com/PerryLink)的一员（40+ 个，全部 Apache-2.0）。如果你在用，**给个 star** —— 它不会解锁任何功能，但会让下一个人在搜索里更容易找到它。 *English:* part of a 40+ plugin family for DeepSeek Harness. If it is useful, **a star helps the next person find it** — nothing is gated behind it. ## What is dsh-permission-rules? Claude Code-style declarative permission rules for DeepSeek Harness. Rules decide what is known. A reviewer model decides what is not. ![Terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules: dsh-permission-rules — deny/ask rules in one YAML file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-hero.png) ![Animated terminal demo of dsh-permission-rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PerryLink/dsh-permission-rules/main/docs/assets/dsh-permission-rules-demo.gif) *The same run, animated.* ## Compatibility | Surface | Status | |---|---| | Harness | DeepSeek Harness `dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1` (adapted 2026-09-22, full gate chain): its plugin config is the live settings contract — every field is declared `.volatile()`, the Loader hands `apply` a live reference per field, and a saved edit is committed into the running references WITHOUT remounting the plugin, with out-of-range values refused by the schema before anything is written. A host whose Schemastery predates `volatile()` (before 3.18.3) still mounts and runs this plugin — the fields simply stay ordinary values and the live config form is unavailable — because the marker is applied through a capability probe rather than assumed. `Session.append` on this line still cannot stamp the `ignorable` marker (its third argument is the surface-intent bag, and the envelope field survives for stored-log reads only), so the whole `0.2-alpha` line is pre-checked as unmarked and session-log audit stays disabled by default — `append` reads only `sourceEventSeqs`/`surfaceOp` and freezes the envelope, so it has no code path that could stamp the marker; the earlier `0.1.7-alpha` (adapted 2026-09-22), `0.1.5-rc.2` (adapted 2026-09-09) and `0.1.3-alpha` lines keep the same surface-only append signature, and every `0.2` prerelease is classified with them (a STABLE `0.2.x` release is left to the append probe, so a restored marker surface is adopted without a new plugin release). Those lines' log migrations refuse unclassified plugin events even when marked, so `strip` v1 audit rows before a `0.1.3-alpha` host opens the log and v2 audit rows before a `0.1.5-alpha` host migrates it (native v3 logs only need `repair`). | | Node | `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0` | | Platforms | All (host + web settings client) | | Model | Any (deny/ask reasons surface through tool results) | ## What you get `dsh-permission-rules` puts an ordered **`allow` / `deny` / `ask`** rule list in front of every tool call on the `tools/pre-execute` waterfall — deterministic, instant, auditable, and written by you in plain YAML: - **`deny`** blocks the call; the rule's `reason` becomes the model-visible error. - **`ask`** rides the official approval seam (mount `dsh-auto-review` for a second-model answerer, or a human answers; with neither, the harness fails closed). - **`allow`** (and no-match) strictly delegates via `next()` — downstream listeners are never short-circuited. Every hit **and** every passthrough is audit-logged as a `permissionRules/decision` session event (log-only — nothing extra is injected into the model context). - **Rich matching** — tool-name globs (including `mcp__*`), agent-identity selectors (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:*`), argument key/value globs **or** regexes (with `!pattern` negation and an `absent` key dimension), workspace-relative path globs at **any nesting depth**, `when` host conditions (env vars, platform), and **shell command decomposition** (`argv`: command word, argument tokens, pipeline signature) for token-precise command matching. - **Built-in high-risk baseline** — a shipped deny/ask ruleset (destructive commands, privilege escalation, download-and-execute, sensitive paths) enabled by default and appended after user rules so a nearer user rule can override it; toggle with `builtin.enabled`. - **Hierarchical rule files** — optional `searchUp` merges every `.dsh/rules.yaml` from the session cwd to the filesystem root, nearest first. - **Dry-run rollout** — `enforce: false` audits what the policy *would* do while passing every call through. - **Hot reload** — Chokidar watch with debounce; a broken edit keeps the previous rules, never crashes. On a WSL host, or for a rule file under `/mnt/`, the watch switches to polling because native change events are unreliable there. - **Fail loud** — invalid YAML, unknown actions/fields, bad globs/regexes, backtracking-prone patterns, or more than `maxRules` rules fail the load. ## Rule syntax ```yaml # /.dsh/rules.yaml rules: - match: { tools: [bash, pwsh], params: { command: "git push*" }, paths: ["**/secrets/**"] } action: deny reason: "No pushes from protected paths" - match: { tools: [edit, write] } action: ask reason: "File writes need confirmation" ``` - **Match dimensions** — `tools` (globs, incl. `mcp__*`), `agents` (`main` / `subagent` / `preset:`; unknown identity never matches — fail closed), `params` (key/value globs or regexes, `!pattern` negation, `absent` key dimension), `paths` (workspace-relative globs extracted at any nesting depth), `when` (`env` var globs/regexes + a closed `platform` list), and `network` (`domains` / `ips` / `ports` / `schemes` — globs, wildcards, CIDRs, port ranges). - **Actions** — `allow` / `deny` / `ask`, evaluated in file order, first match wins. - **Rule metadata** — `enabled: false` (visible but inert), `description`, `tags`; unknown fields fail the load. - **Schema**

plugins.description: DSH 插件：按「会话 × 供应商 × 模型」拆解调用次数与 token 用量，数据只读自 dsh-cost-meter 账本。
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-usage-breakdown

DSH（DeepSeek Harness）插件：**按「会话 × 供应商 × 模型」拆解调用次数与 token 用量**。

一个会话里同时用了 DeepSeek、WorkBuddy、Radeon 好几条路由？面板会告诉你每条路由各被调用了多少次、吃了多少输入/缓存/输出、花了多少钱。

---

## 它解决什么

DSH 本身只告诉你「这一轮花了多少」，`dsh-cost-meter` 告诉你「今天花了多少」。但当你想知道**同一个会话里，究竟是哪个供应商、哪个模型在烧钱**时，这两个都不够。

本插件补的就是这一层：把 cost-meter 的账本重新切成 `会话 → provider:model` 的二维视图，不采集、不写入、不重复计价。

## 功能

- **会话内拆解**：每个会话一张卡片，卡内按 `provider:model` 列出调用次数、输入、缓存读取、输出与成本，横条表示调用量占比
- **当日概览**：会话数、调用次数、输入 token、缓存读取、合计成本
- **日期切换**：可回看账本里任意一天
- **单会话聚焦**：`?session=<id>` 只显示一个会话
- **三种入口**：会话顶部快捷栏、输入框下方、设置 → 插件
- **快捷键**：`Ctrl+Shift+U` 直接打开
- **浮层显示**：面板盖在 DSH 界面里，Esc 或点遮罩关闭

## 前提

需要先安装并运行 **[dsh-cost-meter](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-cost-meter)**，且账本里有数据（`~/.dsh/storages/cost-meter/ledger.json`）。

没有账本时面板会明确提示「找不到账本 + 试过的路径」，而不是空白页。

## 安装

本插件暂未发布到 npm，手动安装：

```bash
# 1. 放进 profile 的 node_modules
git clone https://github.com/qigai74/dsh-usage-breakdown.git \
  ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-usage-breakdown

# 2. 在 profile 的 cordis.patch.yml 末尾追加
#    （~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/cordis.patch.yml）
- insert:
    - id: dsh-usage-breakdown
      name: dsh-usage-breakdown

# 3. 重启 DSH
```

> Windows 路径形如 `C:\Users\<你>\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\`。

## 使用

| 操作 | 行为 |
| --- | --- |
| 左键点「会话用量」 | 只看当前会话 |
| 右键点「会话用量」 | 打开完整面板（当天全部会话） |
| `Ctrl+Shift+U` | 直接打开面板 |
| `Esc` / 点遮罩 | 关闭 |

面板直达地址：`http://127.0.0.1:<DSH端口>/plugins/dsh-usage-breakdown/panel`

> DSH 的 web 端口每次重启都会变，建议用界面入口或快捷键，别收藏固定 URL。

## 数据来源

只读 `~/.dsh/storages/cost-meter/ledger.json` 的这段结构：

```
days["YYYY-MM-DD"]
  ├─ calls / cost / input / cacheRead / output     当日合计
  └─ sessions[]
       └─ { id, calls, cost, input, cacheRead, output,
            byProviderModel: {
              "provider:model": { calls, cost, input, cacheRead, output }
            } }
```

`byProviderModel` 的键就是 `provider:model`，这正是本插件展示的核心维度。

## 设计取舍

**为什么不做采集。** 会话日志解析、增量同步、计价、余额查询，`dsh-cost-meter` 已经做好了，而且是它的本职。本插件只做「另一个视角的展示」，好处是：cost-meter 升级不影响它，两个插件的账本不会打架，也不会出现两份互相矛盾的用量数字。

**为什么不改 cost-meter。** 改第三方插件的代码，升级就丢。只读它的公开数据文件，是一份不会随对方发版失效的契约。

**为什么路由只接受 loopback。** 两个 HTTP 路由都校验 `Host` 是 `127.0.0.1` / `localhost` / `[::1]`，避免被任意网页当作数据源读走账本。

## 已知限制

- 只能按天看，不能跨天汇总同一会话（账本是按天的）
- 面板依赖 `dsh-cost-meter` 的账本格式；若其格式变更，需要同步适配
- 入口依赖宿主的 UI 插槽；若某个版本插槽变更导致按钮不显示，面板仍可通过直达 URL 或 `Ctrl+Shift+U` 访问

## 开发

```
lib/index.js    Host 端：读账本 + 两个路由（/data、/panel）+ 面板页
lib/client.js   浏览器端：入口按钮、浮层、快捷键
```

`lib/client.js` 用 `react.createElement` 而不是 jsx runtime —— 后者的 `jsx(type, props, key)` 第三参数是 `key`，把 children 传进去会让组件渲染成空白，且 `apply`/`register` 全都不报错，极难排查。

调试打点：`lib/client.js` 会在 boot / apply / 每个插槽注册处向 `/plugins/dsh-usage-breakdown/ping` 上报，记录落在 `~/.dsh/.session-usage-ping.log`。

## License

MIT

plugins.description: Codex-style per-step reasoning summaries inside DeepSeek Harness's native thinking disclosure
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-thinking-summary

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

[Source](https://github.com/HUSTforever/dsh-thinking-summary) · MIT · Node.js 22.19+ or 24+

Codex-style per-step reasoning summaries inside DeepSeek Harness's native thinking disclosure. A short action title replaces the raw preview; expanding shows 1–2 sentences and a switch to the original thinking. Answers, tools, images, grouping and disclosure behavior continue to use the native renderer.

Version 0.2 replaces the old end-of-turn card beneath the final answer. It updates during each model step and completes the final snapshot when the step settles. It summarizes high-level actions and findings without reproducing private deliberation or claiming planned actions have succeeded.

Version 0.3 packages the plugin as an installable DSH bundle: a release tarball and Git tag can be installed from the Plugins page or `dsh plugin`, without copying files into the profile. Summary behavior is unchanged from 0.2.

This approximates Codex's presentation. DeepSeek still requires an auxiliary model request, so latency and generation behavior differ from OpenAI's native reasoning-summary stream. See [reasoning summaries](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning) and [streaming events](https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/streaming-events).

## Behavior

- First live update after approximately 1.2 seconds, with at least 40 source characters; the host additionally enforces `minReasoningChars`.
- Further live updates require 8 seconds and 600 new characters. A settled step requests its final snapshot.
- Auxiliary calls are serialized per page and identical requests are coalesced.
- The summary is also rendered as a visible process card beneath the reasoning row, so the body is readable without expanding the disclosure; the disclosure keeps the short title and can still switch to the original thinking.
- Historical rows backfill automatically once they enter or approach the viewport; scrolling fills them lazily instead of starting a whole-session batch.
- Failed summaries can be retried. Original thinking remains accessible through the official reasoning body slot, including other body presentation plugins.
- Summaries follow the DSH locale by default. Open **Plugins → Installed plugins → dsh-thinking-summary** to choose the summary model; set the language to `auto` to follow DSH or enter a tag such as `zh`, `en`, or `zh-CN`. The prompt asks for Codex's `**action heading** + 1–2 sentences` format, grounded in the user request, tool activity/results, and answer rather than only the private trace.
- No session events or model-visible messages are modified. The browser creates display-only copies of reasoning blocks.
- Cache identity includes provider, model, locale and exact text; host cache also includes prompt version and output settings. Old retrospective summaries are not reused for the new format.

## Install

The plugin installs as a DSH bundle: its manifest points at `cordis.patch.yml`,
so the plugin manager downloads the package, adds it to the profile's bundle
list, and applies the defaults. No file copying and no manual profile edit are
required.

Tested with Harness desktop `0.2.1-rc.2`; the package declares
`engines.dsh: ">=0.2.1-rc.2"`.

### From the Plugins page (desktop and Web)

1. Open **Plugins** in the sidebar.
2. Choose **Add plugin**, then **Install a third-party plugin**.
3. Paste one of these specs:
   - Release tarball:
     `https://github.com/HUSTforever/dsh-thinking-summary/releases/download/v0.3.0/dsh-thinking-summary-0.3.0.tgz`
   - Git tag: `github:HUSTforever/dsh-thinking-summary#v0.3.0`
4. Install, then choose **Enable now** if the dialog offers it.
5. Open **Plugins → Installed plugins → dsh-thinking-summary** to pick the
   summary model and language.

The bundle supplies the defaults (`language: auto`, `thinking: off`,
`maxChars: 600`), so nothing needs to be added to the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml`.

### From the CLI (web, TUI and headless profiles)

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <spec>
```

Pass the same tarball URL or Git spec as above. The desktop profile is owned by
the desktop app, so install there through the Plugins page instead.

### Manual installation (development only)

To test local changes without installing the bundle, copy `package.json`,
`cordis.patch.yml`, `lib/` and the README/CHANGELOG/LICENSE files into:

```text
%USERPROFILE%\.dsh\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-thinking-summary
```

and add the insert entry from [cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml) to the
profile's `cordis.patch.yml`. Do not do this on a profile where the bundle is
already installed — the entry would be inserted twice.

### Updating

Third-party bundles upgrade by removing the installed copy and installing the
newer spec; the Plugins page offers this as uninstall followed by install. Tags
give every release a stable spec, for example
`github:HUSTforever/dsh-thinking-summary#v0.3.0`.

Profile configuration can reload live. After replacing already-imported
JavaScript, refresh the page (and restart Harness if the host half changed) to
load both halves. The local port may change; check
`/dsh-thinking-summary/health` on the current port.

## Plugin settings

Open **Plugins → Installed plugins → dsh-thinking-summary**, then use the **Thinking summary** section on the plugin's detail page to choose the summary provider/model (or follow the conversation route) and the language (`auto` follows DSH; `zh`, `en`, `zh-CN`, etc. override it). Settings are saved to `~/.dsh/thinking-summary/settings.json` and apply immediately.

## Configuration

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `provider`, `model` | empty | Use the route recorded for the step; configure both as a host fallback if needed. |
| `language` | `auto` | Follow the DSH locale; overridable in the plugin settings. |
| `thinking` | `off` | Disable thinking for the auxiliary request, falling back if unsupported. |
| `maxChars` | `600` | Combined title/body character budget. |
| `maxOutputTokens` | `220` | Auxiliary output token cap. |
| `minReasoningChars` | `120` | Shorter sources skip generation. |
| `maxInputChars` | `24000` | Keep the head and tail of longer inputs. |
| `timeoutMs` | `45000` | Per-generation deadline. |
| `cacheSize` | `400` | Host cache entries; `0` disables caching. |

Durable cache: `~/.dsh/thinking-summary/cache.json`; plugin settings: `~/.dsh/thinking-summary/settings.json`. Clearing the cache does not alter sessions.

## Version management

`package.json` is the single source of the version; the health route reads it when the host half loads, so a release bump never edits two places. Work lands on `main`, and every release is a semver tag:

```powershell
npm version patch --message "release: v%s"   # or minor / major
git push --follow-tags
```

`npm version` updates `package.json`, commits and creates the annotated `vX.Y.Z` tag. Push it with `git push --follow-tags`; the Release workflow then runs the checks, packs `dsh-thinking-summary-X.Y.Z.tgz` and creates the GitHub release with that tarball attached. Every release is installable from its asset URL or its Git tag. CI runs `npm run check` and `npm test` on every push and pull request.

## Development

No build step or dependencies are required. The browser bundle only imports the baseline `react` module and receives Harness services through the plugin context.

```powershell
npm test
npm run check
```

plugins.description: DeepSeek Harness plugin: a Settings-resident WeChat daily report. Reads local WeChat 4.x databases read-only, ranks the day's chats, and separates what needs you from what to ignore.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-wechat-daily · 微信日报

一个装进 **DeepSeek Harness** 设置页的微信日报插件：每天结束前，把本机微信里发生的事整理成一份日报，
分成 **需要处理**、**值得一看**、**可以忽略** 三段；同时在对话里给 agent 一个 `wechat_daily_report` 工具。

只读微信本地数据库，不发消息、不改数据。解密、排序、渲染全部在本机完成；模型那一步是可选的开关。

```
设置 → 微信日报
─────────────────────────────────────────────
微信日报
每天结束前，把微信里发生的事整理成一份日报。

[已绑定微信数据库 · 1] [今天 · 2026-10-20] [下次自动生成 · 21:30] [立即生成日报]

# 微信日报 · 2026-10-19 周一
> 今天共 186 条消息，来自 23 个会话；3 件事可能要你处理。
**导师叫你去办公室，还有人问能不能上课，两件都等你回应**
## 需要处理
1. **王老师** — 问开题报告什么时候给他，说周一要拿去评审
   - 为什么重要：有明确截止时间，且导师在等
   - 你要做：周日晚前把初稿发邮件给王老师
…
```

## 特性

- **只看该看的**：私聊、@我、被点名、涉及钱/截止/请求的消息往上抬；服务号、外卖券群、刷屏群往下压。
- **模型可选**：开着由模型写摘要与分类；关掉只走本地规则，一条消息都不出本机。
- **定时**：默认每天 21:30 生成，可改；错过的当天会在启动后补一次。
- **可追溯**：日报以 Markdown + JSON 存在 `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-wechat-daily/reports/`，随时可删。
- **只读**：解密到本机缓存后只做 SELECT；不写回微信容器，不需要关闭 SIP。

## 安装

前置：macOS（微信 4.x 桌面版）、Node ≥ 23.4（需要内置 `node:sqlite`）、已装 DeepSeek Harness。

```sh
git clone https://github.com/zengpu987-ctrl/dsh-wechat-daily.git
```

然后在 DSH 里安装这个目录：

```text
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target=/absolute/path/to/dsh-wechat-daily
```

装好后 **设置 → 微信日报** 会出现一页。首次打开会显示「尚未绑定微信数据库」——下面这步只做一次。

## 一次性密钥捕获

微信 4.x 的消息库是 WCDB / SQLCipher 4，密钥不在任何磁盘文件里明文保存，只在打开数据库的瞬间经过
`CCKeyDerivationPBKDF`。所以要取一次密钥，之后每天只读数据库。

流程（脚本在 `tools/keycapture/`，原理见 [docs/key-capture.md](docs/key-capture.md)）：

1. 正常退出微信（菜单「退出」，不要强杀）。
2. 复制 `/Applications/WeChat.app` 到临时目录，**只对副本**做 ad-hoc 重签——原版一个字节都不动。
3. 用 lldb 以父进程方式启动副本，在 `sqlite3_key` / `CCKeyDerivationPBKDF` / `PKCS5_PBKDF2_HMAC`
   上记录参数并自动继续。
4. 认出多库复用的那把主密钥，用它派生每库密钥，逐个用第 1 页 HMAC 验证。
5. 关掉副本、删临时目录、重新打开原版微信。

产物是 `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-wechat-daily/keys.json`（权限 600），只放主密钥与派生缓存。
**这个文件不要提交、不要上传、不要放进同步盘。**

> 微信换密钥（重装、重新登录、大版本改动方案）后需要重新捕获。多个微信账号各有主密钥，需分别捕获。

## 配置

设置页里可以改：是否每天自动生成、生成时间、是否让模型写摘要、我的昵称（用于识别点名）、关注关键词。
值存在 `~/.dsh/storages/dsh-wechat-daily/config.json`。

agent 工具：

| action | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `status` | 密钥是否已绑定、今天是否已生成、下次生成时间 |
| `generate` | 立即生成（可带 `date: YYYY-MM-DD`） |
| `latest` | 读出现成的日报正文 |

## 它是怎么读数据的

1. 账号主密钥 + 每个库自己的 salt → 派生该库密钥（PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512，256000 轮）。
2. 先给数据库和它的 `-wal` 做快照，再逐页解密到缓存；WAL 帧只在 SQLite 校验链完整时才应用，
   合并结果过 `quick_check`，不通过就退回主库镜像——宁可少最后几条，也不返回损坏数据。
3. `node:sqlite` 只读查询 `Msg_<md5(username)>` 表，按 `Name2Id` 还原发言人，按 `contact` 还原会话名，
   按 `WCDB_CT_message_content` 判断 zstd 压缩并解压。

## 文件地图

| 文件 | 职责 |
|---|---|
| `lib/sqlcipher.mjs` | SQLCipher 4 只读解密、HMAC 校验、WAL 帧合并 |
| `lib/wechat.mjs` | 账号发现、快照、表结构与消息解析 |
| `lib/digest.mjs` | 会话排序、提示词、模型 JSON 解析 |
| `lib/report.mjs` | 编排、渲染、落盘 |
| `index.js` | HTTP 路由、定时、agent 工具 |
| `client.js` | 设置页（React，无构建步骤） |
| `tools/keycapture/` | lldb / 内存扫描取密钥脚本 |
| `docs/example-report.md` | 虚构的日报样例（不含任何真实聊天） |

## 测试

```sh
node --test "test/*.test.mjs"
```

`test/sqlcipher.test.mjs` 会按 WCDB 的真实页格式自行加密一份数据库（含 WAL 帧与校验链），
再验证解密、HMAC、WAL 合并与「尾部被写坏时不污染页面」；`test/digest.test.mjs` 覆盖排序、
点名识别、JSON 容错与长度预算。不需要微信、不需要密钥。

## 已知限制

- 只处理文本类消息；图片、语音、视频、表情只记成 `[图片]` 之类的占位。
- 只读本机已同步的聊天；手机上未迁移到电脑的历史不在这里。
- 每个微信账号一份主密钥，多账号需分别捕获；未绑定账号会被跳过（页面显示 `hasKey: false`）。
- 日报质量取决于所选模型；模型不可用时自动退回本地规则版并标注原因。

## 隐私与免责

- 解密、排序、渲染全在本机；只有你打开「让模型写摘要」时，被选中会话的摘要才会发给当前模型。
- 请勿在 issue 里粘贴 `keys.json`、真实 `wxid`、聊天截图或完整日报。
- 本项目用于**本人设备上本人账号**的数据整理。在部分司法辖区，绕过客户端加密可能受限；
  微信更新也可能使流程失效。作者不对使用后果负责，详见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)。

## License

MIT © 2026 Zeng pu

plugins.description: Guarded GitHub tools for DeepSeek Harness: 9 typed github_* tools (58 actions) where every state-changing action needs confirm:true plus a human approval seam, with a digest-verified self-update and a settings page. Zero runtime dependencies. | 面向 DSH 的 GitHub 工具：所有写动作都过审批门
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-github-gate

**GitHub tools for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) where a write cannot happen by accident.** 9 typed `github_*` tools over the GitHub CLI, 61 actions in all. 29 of them are marked destructive and need `confirm: true` **and** a human approval seam; the four write methods `github_api` accepts are classified at run time. The model's flag is intent; it is not consent. ```text github_pr { action: "merge", number: 42, confirm: true } → an approval prompt naming the pull request; "no" stops it → after consent: gh pr merge 42 --repo owner/name ``` - **Argv arrays, never a shell.** `gh` is spawned with `shell: false`, so model text cannot become shell syntax — structurally, not by filtering. - **One credential chain, resolved per call.** DSH credential store → `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` → `gh auth login` → git credential helper. Rotating a token applies to the next call. - **Configuration in the GUI.** Settings → Plugins → GitHub: paste a PAT, test it against the API, see which layer is live. The token is never displayed back. - **A branch pill** in the session header: current branch, its pull request, and a switch menu that fails closed when the caller cannot be judged. - **Digest-verified self-update.** `github_update` stages a release whose sha256 is checked against the digest GitHub publishes. Host-side tools plus one small browser half. 0 runtime dependencies. No build step. > **Requires** DeepSeek Harness `>=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0` and the > [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (`gh`) on `PATH`. Linux, macOS, and Windows. **Topics:** `dsh-plugin` · `deepseek-harness` · `dsh` · `cordis-plugin` · `github` · `gh-cli` ## Why this over another GitHub plugin Tool count is a bad proxy for usefulness — a broader surface with looser gates is easier to write and harder to trust. The trade this project makes is explicit: | | Other GitHub plugins for DSH | This one | |---|---|---| | Write safety | `confirm: true`, set by the model | `confirm: true` **+** an approval seam the model cannot set | | Raw REST | unrestricted escape hatch | path must be relative, no `..`, write methods gated at run time | | Correctness evidence | tests of its own API | 207 tests, 180 behaviour snapshots, and **84 argv shapes parsed by a real `gh`** | | Failure messages | HTTP code passed through | 401 / 403 quota / 403 SSO / 404 / 422 each name the fix | | Scope | as many tools as possible | 9 tools / 61 actions, one to a `gh` subcommand family | | Self-update | — | staged with a verified sha256, install left to the platform | If you want the largest possible tool surface with no gates, this is not the right plugin. If you want the model to be able to *look* at GitHub freely but need a person in the loop before it *changes* anything, it is. ## Table of contents - [Install](#install) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Guidance](#guidance) - [The branch pill](#the-branch-pill) - [Settings page](#settings-page) - [What it provides](#what-it-provides) - [Updating this plugin](#updating-this-plugin) - [Configuration](#configuration) - [Credential chain](#credential-chain) - [Device Flow needs your own OAuth App](#device-flow-needs-your-own-oauth-app) - [Safety model](#safety-model) - [Background jobs](#background-jobs) - [Known limitations](#known-limitations) - [Development](#development) ## Install Two ways, both through the Harness plugin manager (`plugin_manager` action `install_bundle`): 1. **From a GitHub release** — download `dsh-github-gate-.tgz` from [Releases](../../releases) and point `install_bundle` at the unpacked package directory, or at a local path holding it. 2. **From a packed tarball of your own checkout**: ```bash npm pack --pack-destination ../packages # pack OUTSIDE the source directory ``` then install `../packages/dsh-github-gate-.tgz`. **Install from a packed tarball, not from the source directory.** This is not a style preference. Installing a `link:` to a workspace directory produces a junction, and the launcher's runtime resolution does not reach bare `@deepseek-ai/*` packages through it — the plugin then fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and refuses to activate entirely. Pack the tarball **outside** the source tree: one run that packed into the source directory itself left that directory emptied once the install completed (see [docs/DESIGN.md](./docs/DESIGN.md) §5.8). The tarball is a snapshot, so editing the source requires repacking and reinstalling; a restart loads the new module generation. ### One-command download The install scripts fetch the latest release, verify its sha256 against the digest GitHub publishes, and print the install path. They deliberately do not install — that step belongs to the plugin manager, which asks for approval: ```powershell # Windows irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1273984347/dsh-github-gate/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` ```sh # Linux / macOS curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/1273984347/dsh-github-gate/main/install.sh | sh ``` Then install the printed path with `plugin_manager` action `install_bundle`. ## Quick start ```text 1. Is there a credential? github_auth { action: "status" } credential source: credentials-seam | environment | gh-cli | git-credential-helper | none 2. No credential? Establish one. github_auth { action: "login" } # Device Flow, needs your own OAuth App — or paste a PAT in Settings → Plugins → GitHub — or just run `gh auth login` in a terminal; the chain picks it up 3. Something is broken? github_auth { action: "probe" } # isolates each layer, names the failed one 4. Work on a pull request. github_pr { action: "status" } # CI for the branch you are on github_pr { action: "view", number: 42 } github_pr { action: "checks", number: 42 } github_pr { action: "merge", number: 42, confirm: true } # asks a person ``` The repository is taken from the workspace's git remote when `repo` is omitted, so the common case needs no argument. ## Guidance Beyond the tools, this plugin contributes a **prompt section** and three **skills** that say what the tool schemas cannot: when to use which capability, what evidence a conclusion needs, and when to stop. The rules are deliberately few — a prompt section is paid for on every step — and each one names the tool it applies to. Three workflows load on demand: `github-pr-review`, `github-ci-triage`, `github-issue-to-pr`. ## The branch pill `client.js` is the browser half: a branch pill in the session header slot (`conversation.session.header.utilities`) showing the checked-out branch, the pull request open on it, and a menu for switching branches. It is ~26 KB and it is the only part of this bundle that renders in the browser. It reads through four loopback HTTP routes this plugin registers on the `webServer` service: | Route | Does | Without a `connection` service | |---|---|---| | `/branch`, `/branches`, `/diagnostics` | read the workspace and branch names | served, with one logged warning | | `/switch` | runs `git switch` on the working tree | **refused with 403** | A missing service is not consent: an apparatus that cannot judge a request must not treat "cannot judge" as "judged safe". The read routes fail open because re

plugins.readme_text:
# 操作约定注入（dsh-ops-conventions）

把「操作约定」在**动手前**确定性注入上下文，解决「约定记了但干活时不提就不用」的问题。

## 它做什么

- **版本变化后下一轮就注入，不再等下一个操作轮**：不按「像不像要动手」过滤，闲聊轮也会注入；每会话每版本只注入一次（约 150 token）。
- **门铃自带 6 行常驻约定**：收尾三件（自检/记忆归并/`_tasks` 清空）、不列多方案、备份回滚、只改工具区、关会话提醒等直接写进门铃，不再依赖可能被 OpenViking 抽取重写的 `profile.md` 段。
- **同一会话同版本只注入一次**：不刷屏。
- **约定版本变化自动再提醒**：改 `VERSION` 后，下一轮（任何类型）会重新注入。
- **注入日志**：每次注入记一行（含选中的约定目录、索引是否存在），生效与否可核对。
- **硬拦截（默认开）**：操作类轮次里，本会话还没 `read` 过 `INDEX.md` 时，`write`/`edit` 等写类工具会被直接拒绝，并提示先读索引；读过后本会话放行。闲聊轮次不拦；shell 默认不拦（可配置）。
- **零配置可用**：包内自带 `skills/` 示例清单；也可以指向你自己的目录，或 OpenViking 里存的那份。

## 为什么会有这个插件

作者是一名 DSH 日常用户（学生，用 DSH + OpenViking 管理学习和工具工作流），遇到的问题很具体：

- 把「写脚本前先看清单」「改文件前先备份」这类操作约定写进了 OpenViking 技能和记忆；
- 但真正干活时，模型并不会稳定地主动去读它们——**约定记了，干活时不提就不用**，等于白记；
- 靠提示词或 `AGENTS.md` 也不稳：要么每轮全量注入太费 token，要么模型想起来才看。

于是和 AI 助手一起做了这个小插件：每会话每版本注入一条极短的门铃（入口清单路径 + 版本号），约定版本一改，下一轮就重新出现——不等到「像要动手」的那一轮。后来发现「注入了也可能不执行」，就补了硬拦截：操作类轮次里没读索引前，写操作直接过不去。

**关于代码**：需求、取舍、验证由作者决定；具体实现是与 AI 助手协作完成的。

**为什么公开**：相信「约定记了但干活不提就不用」不是个例，才把它整理出来上传，希望能帮到有同样需求的人。如果你遇到同样的问题，欢迎直接拿去用，也欢迎把你的场景告诉我，一起改进。

## 安装

### 方式一：安装脚本（推荐，跨平台、零依赖）

```bash
git clone https://github.com/HeliosTangDev/dsh-ops-conventions.git
cd dsh-ops-conventions
node install.mjs                       # 默认装到 ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop
node install.mjs /path/to/profile      # 指定 profile
node install.mjs /path/to/profile --uninstall   # 卸载
```

它会：复制到 `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ops-conventions`、在 `package.json` 的 `dependencies` 登记、把包名加进 `dsh.profile.bundles`（不加不会被加载）。

### 方式二：手动

1. 把整个仓库复制到 `<profile>/node_modules/dsh-ops-conventions`；
2. 编辑 `<profile>/package.json`：
   ```json
   "dependencies": { "dsh-ops-conventions": "0.2.0" },
   "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": [ ..., "dsh-ops-conventions" ] } }
   ```

> 注意：`package.json` 里必须有 `dsh.bundle.patch` 指向 `cordis.patch.yml`（本包已带）。缺了它，插件管理器会报「没有声明组合包」，且**不会被加载**。

### 装完

- **热重载**：DSH 插件页 → 找到 `dsh-ops-conventions` → 关掉再打开（改 `skills/` 或配置时不用重启）。
- 改的是**代码**（`index.mjs` / `rule.mjs`）时，关掉再打开不保证重新 import，**重启 DeepSeek Harness** 最稳。

## 配置

| 配置项 | 环境变量 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `skillsDir` | `DSH_OPS_CONVENTIONS_DIR` | 包内 `skills/` | 约定目录，需含 `INDEX.md`；`VERSION` 可有可无 |
| `logFile` | `DSH_OPS_CONVENTIONS_LOG` | `~/.dsh/ops-conventions/ops-conventions.log` | 注入 / 拦截日志 |
| `enforce` | — | `true` | 是否启用硬拦截；`false` = 只注入门铃 |
| `blockedTools` | — | `write` `edit` `multi_edit` `apply_patch` `notebook_edit` | 拦截的写类工具名；要连 shell 一起拦就自行加 `bash` / `pwsh` |

解析顺序（会**逐个检查目录里真的有 `INDEX.md`**，取第一个有效的）：

1. 配置项 `skillsDir`
2. 环境变量 `DSH_OPS_CONVENTIONS_DIR`
3. **包内 `skills/`**（随包发布，开箱即用）
4. OpenViking 实际存储：`~/.openviking/data/viking/default/user/default/memories/ops-conventions`
5. `~/.dsh/ops-conventions/skills`

示例（写进 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`）：

```yaml
- id: dsh-ops-conventions
  name: "dsh-ops-conventions"
  config:
    skillsDir: "D:/my-conventions/skills"
    enforce: true
    # blockedTools: ["write", "edit", "bash"]
```

## 约定目录结构

```
skills/
├── INDEX.md          # 入口清单（注入文本里给的就是它的路径）
├── VERSION           # 版本号；改它 → 下一次操作轮重新注入
└── ops-scripts/
    └── SKILL.md      # 各类清单，INDEX.md 里引用
```

自带 6 类示例：`ops-scripts`（脚本/后台）、`ops-notes`（笔记）、`ops-files`（文件目录）、`ops-check`（自检）、`ops-longtask`（长任务）、`ops-dsh`（DSH/插件）。可以直接改成你自己的。

## 机制

- 监听 `agent/pre-step`（waterfall），在模型调用前判断最后一条用户消息像不像"要动手"（工具词 或 动作词+对象词）。
- 命中且该会话该版本未注入过 → 追加一条 `instructions` 来源的消息。
- **硬拦截**监听 `tools/pre-execute`（waterfall）：当轮用户消息像要动手、且本会话还没**成功** `read` 过 `INDEX.md` 时，对写类工具返回 `deny`（理由里带索引绝对路径），模型照做后重试即可通过；`tools/result` 观察成功的 INDEX 读取后放行。
- 钩子自身异常一律 **fail-open**（放行）并写日志；`skillsDir` 里没有 `INDEX.md` 时不拦。
- 任何异常都吞掉，不影响正常对话；多会话各自独立判断。
- 日志里可核对：`inject vN`、`guard deny`、`guard index-read`、`guard loaded enforce=...`。

## 常见问题

**Q：插件市场里搜不到？**
A：市场只索引 npm / GitHub 上的包，本地安装的不会出现在搜索结果里；在「已装」列表里能看到。

**Q：卡片显示「异常：这个包没有声明组合包」？**
A：`package.json` 缺 `dsh.bundle.patch`。本包已带；如果你自己改了包，记得保留。

**Q：模型说 `skill xxx is unknown`？**
A：那是会话启动时的技能目录快照导致的，与插件无关。直接用 `read` 读注入里给的那个 `INDEX.md` 路径即可。

**Q：写文件被拒绝，理由是「硬拦截」？**
A：本会话还没 `read` 过 `INDEX.md`。按理由里给的路径读一次（并执行对应清单），再重试原操作即可；不想要这个行为，把配置 `enforce` 设为 `false`。

**Q：注入的提醒会显示在对话里？**
A：会，作为一条来源为插件的消息。长度约 70 token，一个会话只出现一次（版本变了再一次）。

## License

MIT

## Star

如果这个插件对你有用，欢迎在 GitHub 上点个 ⭐ Star，让更多 DSH 用户看到。

# Blender Mentor **Turn Claude Code / DSH / Cursor into a senior Blender mentor + technical director.** It diagnoses your level, teaches a structured lesson, grades your work with a 0–3 rubric, and runs machine acceptance on your `.blend` — assets, curves, renders, ESD secondary animation, and biomechanics. **English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) [![validate-skill](https://github.com/Memory175/blender-mentor/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Memory175/blender-mentor/actions) [![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Memory175/blender-mentor?color=2f81f7)](https://github.com/Memory175/blender-mentor/releases) [![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Memory175/blender-mentor?color=3fb950)](https://github.com/Memory175/blender-mentor/blob/main/LICENSE) [![last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/Memory175/blender-mentor?color=8b5cf6)](https://github.com/Memory175/blender-mentor/commits/main) [![Blender](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blender-4.2%20LTS%20%7C%205.x-orange)](https://www.blender.org/download/) ## What it looks like ```text you › Review this walk cycle. Grade it with the rubric and give me a P0/P1/P2 fix list. mentor › L2 · Review mode · score 2.1 / 3 — critical: foot sliding P0 Lock contact frames 1 / 13 / 25; add heel roll. P1 Reduce hip Y translation 18%; clean shoulder counter-rotation. P2 Add toe flex on push-off; re-check the 12-frame cadence. acceptance asset_gate PASS · curve_audit 3 warnings · render_probe PASS ``` ![Example session: prompt, rubric score, P0/P1/P2 fixes, machine acceptance](docs/demo.svg) > **Not a Blender add-on.** The skill gives your AI agent the mentor's playbook. It can generate commands and, when the host has shell/Blender access (or an MCP bridge), run `blender -b ... --python ...` automatically. Without that access it cannot operate Blender's UI for you. You still need Blender installed to open `.blend` files and run acceptance checks (see [Requirements](#requirements)). ## Rubric at a glance | Score | Meaning | Walk-cycle example | |---|---|---| | **0** | A critical item vetoes the delivery | foot sliding → 0, not deliverable regardless of the other items | | **2** | Shippable | contacts locked, no interpenetration | | **3** | Production-ready | contacts locked + heel roll + reusable cadence | Full scoring anchors and self-review template: [`references/rubric.md`](references/rubric.md). ## Quick start **DSH** — clone and install (Windows / Linux / macOS / WSL): ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Memory175/blender-mentor.git cd blender-mentor # Windows powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File dsh/install.ps1 # Linux / macOS / WSL bash dsh/install.sh ``` **Claude Code** — install as a plugin: ```text /plugin marketplace add Memory175/blender-mentor /plugin install blender-mentor@blender-mentor-marketplace ``` **Cursor / other Agent Skills clients** — clone the repo and point your client at `SKILL.md` (in Cursor, mention `@SKILL.md`; for an always-on rule, add a project rule that references it). Then open a new agent session and try: ```text Use blender-mentor to walk me through M1 modeling and topology. ``` ## What you get | Component | What it does | |---|---| | **Mentor behavior** | L0–L3 level diagnosis; explain / coach / accept / firefight / review modes | | **D1–D4 delivery loop** | deliver → self-review → P0/P1/P2 fix list → explicit next-step question | | **0–3 rubric** | critical items, scoring anchors, and a self-review template | | **Engineering precheck (ENG-001)** | stability, wall thickness, draft, overhang/support, interference, clearance | | **M0–M6 curriculum** | modeling & topology → UV/materials/lighting/render → animation/rigging → physics/geometry nodes/pipeline | | **24 executable tools** | 6 `.blend` acceptance scripts + engineering precheck + module governance (preflight/lint/conflict/claim audit/self-audit index) + source governance (audit/refresh) + regression/routing tools | | **Delivery QA gate** | floors/coordinates, mesh/UV, camera/export, professional-boundary checks | | **INT-001 (experimental)** | Chinese-style two-bedroom apartment interior; declares `styles`/`layouts`; sources pending | | **INT-002 (experimental)** | modern luxury large flat; program from user plan; dimensions pending | | **Interior rule** | interior modeling requires a dedicated `INT-*` module with `styles`/`layouts`; style/layout mismatches are surfaced | | **Knowledge base** | 130 common misconceptions + 40 red lines | ## Requirements | Requirement | Needed for | |---|---| | Blender 4.2 LTS / 5.x | `.blend` acceptance scripts (`blender -b ... --python scripts/...`) | | Python 3 | `selftest.py`, `persona_lint.py`, `load_router.py`, `preflight.py` | | Optional: shell or Blender MCP/RT bridge | Automatic script execution; without it, copy commands into Blender Scripting or a terminal manually | ## How it works ```text SKILL.md routing + D1–D4 delivery loop + machine-acceptance commands references/ 14 reference files (9 persona docs + module format + authoring guide + model QA + INT modules), loaded on demand scripts/ 24 executable tools assets/ ESD templates, load plans, deny-word example, source registry template ``` 1. `SKILL.md` routes the request and sets the delivery loop. 2. `preflight.py` classifies it: `proceed` (module-backed), `proceed_core` (teaching/operations, no module needed), `ask`, or `block` (reference data required but not covered). 3. `load_router.py` builds a per-task load plan and only loads modules selected by preflight; `proceed_core` tasks get core docs, never modules. 4. `source_audit.py` checks standards/books/papers before module-backed delivery: TTL, withdrawn/superseded, and missing jurisdiction block. 5. Acceptance scripts run against your local `.blend` through headless Blender. 6. Your files stay local; the acceptance tools do not upload anything.
Advanced installation ### Claude.ai Zip the skill folder (`SKILL.md` + `references/`, `scripts/`, `assets/`) and add it to your Skills library. ### DSH plugin market This repository is also a DSH skill plugin: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch → cordis.patch.yml`, which mounts the bundled `skills/blender-mentor/`. After the dsh.so listing is approved: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:Memory175/blender-mentor ``` ### Downloadable installers `dsh-install.ps1` and `dsh-install.sh` are attached to the [latest release](https://github.com/Memory175/blender-mentor/releases/latest); download and run them if you prefer not to clone.

plugins.description: A DSH plugin that turns one provider API key into a managed pool + more built-in LLM Providers
plugins.readme_text:
# DSH Keys Manager

[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-keys-manager)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-339933)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%5E0.2.1--rc.2-0969DA)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm)

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns one provider API key into a managed pool.
It extends the Models page rather than replacing it: providers, models, and the
model picker stay where they are; only the API-key source moves behind the
manager.

## Features

- Several keys per provider, each with an alias and health state.
- One key pinned to a session, with round-robin selection for new sessions.
- Bounded retry on the same key, then automatic failover to another key.
- Exponential cooldown recovery, capped at seven days.
- A search-driven Keys Manager page on the plugin's own detail page.
- A "managed by Keys Manager" badge inside the existing Models provider cards.
- Extra built-in providers installed as ordinary `llm-pi-ai` routes.
- OAuth account sign-in for seven pi-ai-backed providers, stored beside
  the API keys.

### Extra providers

This catalog of 35 extra providers comes from
[oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)'s provider catalog (MIT).

<details>
<summary>All 35 extra providers</summary>

| Provider | Route id | API key env |
|---|---|---|
| DeepInfra | `deepinfra` | `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY` |
| Novita | `novita` | `NOVITA_API_KEY` |
| StepFun | `stepfun` | `STEPFUN_API_KEY` |
| SambaNova | `sambanova` | `SAMBANOVA_API_KEY` |
| Qianfan | `qianfan` | `QIANFAN_API_KEY` |
| GMI Cloud | `gmi-cloud` | `GMI_API_KEY` |
| Synthetic | `synthetic` | `SYNTHETIC_API_KEY` |
| ZenMux | `zenmux` | `ZENMUX_API_KEY` |
| Kilo Gateway | `kilo` | `KILO_API_KEY` |
| NanoGPT | `nanogpt` | `NANO_GPT_API_KEY` |
| Venice AI | `venice` | `VENICE_API_KEY` |
| AIML API | `aimlapi` | `AIMLAPI_API_KEY` |
| AI& | `aiand` | `AIAND_API_KEY` |
| Helmcode | `helmcode` | `HELMCODE_API_KEY` |
| Alibaba Coding Plan | `alibaba-coding-plan` | `ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| MiniMax Coding (Global) | `minimax-code` | `MINIMAX_CODE_API_KEY` |
| MiniMax Coding (CN) | `minimax-code-cn` | `MINIMAX_CODE_CN_API_KEY` |
| Umans AI Coding Plan | `umans` | `UMANS_AI_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| Sakana AI | `sakana` | `SAKANA_API_KEY` |
| CoralBricks | `coralbricks` | `CORAL_API_KEY` |
| Wafer Serverless | `wafer-serverless` | `WAFER_SERVERLESS_API_KEY` |
| Alibaba Token Plan | `alibaba-token-plan` | `ALIBABA_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| Alibaba Token Plan (CN) | `alibaba-token-plan-cn` | `BAILIAN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| Charm Hyper | `charm-hyper` | `CHARM_HYPER_API_KEY`, `HYPER_API_KEY` |
| LiteLLM Proxy | `litellm` | `LITELLM_API_KEY` |
| SiliconFlow | `siliconflow` | `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY` |
| SiliconFlow (CN) | `siliconflow-cn` | `SILICONFLOW_CN_API_KEY` |
| Zhipu Coding Plan | `zhipu-coding-plan` | `ZHIPU_API_KEY` |
| Abliteration | `abliteration` | `ABLITERATION_API_KEY`, `ABLIT_KEY` |
| ClinePass | `cline-pass` | `CLINE_API_KEY` |
| Command Code | `commandcode` | `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY`, `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` |
| CoreWeave Serverless Inference | `coreweave` | `COREWEAVE_API_KEY` |
| Fire Pass | `firepass` | `FIREPASS_API_KEY` |
| Ollama Cloud | `ollama-cloud` | `OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` |
| Yolo Auto | `yolo-auto` | `YOLO_AUTO_API_KEY` |

Where two variables are listed, either is accepted; the first is the primary.

CoreWeave Serverless Inference also needs `COREWEAVE_PROJECT=<team>/<project>` in the DSH process environment before it is added.

</details>

## Quick start

### Install — DeepSeek Harness Desktop / Web

In the DeepSeek Harness Desktop or Web app, open **Plugins**, click
**Add plugin**, enter `dsh-keys-manager` in the package field, and click
**Install**. When the install finishes, choose **Enable now** so the plugin is
switched on.

Through the wizard, the app installs the same published npm package as the
CLI path below, already carrying its built bundle. Refresh the DeepSeek
Harness page afterwards so the browser half is fetched.

### Install — published package

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-keys-manager
```

### Install — local checkout

```sh
git clone https://github.com/btspoony/dsh-keys-manager
cd dsh-keys-manager
pnpm i
dsh plugin --profile web link .
```

The two CLI paths differ in where the build output comes from: `dsh plugin
--profile web add dsh-keys-manager` installs the published npm tarball, which
ships the built `lib/` and the client bundle. The local
`dsh plugin --profile web link .` path runs `prepare` during `pnpm i`, which
builds `lib/` and the client bundle, so the clone flow above includes that
build step; `prepack` builds the same output when the package is packed or
published.

Refresh the Web page after installing so the browser half is fetched.

## Usage

Open **Plugins → Keys Manager → View** (rendered as
`Plugins → 密钥管理 → 查看` in the Chinese locale). The manager renders on the
plugin's detail page, between its description and its included rows, matching
the shipped plugin configuration cards.

1. Search for a provider. Existing DSH providers appear first; the plugin also
   ships the curated extra catalog described above.
2. Adopt a provider. For an existing provider the manager imports the
   currently resolved credential, writes a broker reference into the provider
   profile, and leaves the original key in the credential store so release can
   restore it.
3. Add more keys with an alias. Every key is stored in the Harness credential
   store under its own reference; the manager state document never contains a
   key literal.
4. Manage a key from the three-dot menu: rename, pause/resume, delete. A key
   row shows status, last use, and the recovery time while cooling.
5. Tune retry count (1–3), base cooldown, and recovery grace in the settings
   card.

### OAuth accounts

Providers that ship a native OAuth sign-in offer two ways to join the pool:
**Add key** stores a static API key, while **Add account** runs the
provider's OAuth sign-in flow and stores the resulting grant as an account
row in the same pool.

Supported providers — the seven whose OAuth flows `llm-pi-ai` implements:
Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Coding, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, Radius,
and xAI.

The increment-1 model is honest about scope: **API keys form the selection
ring** — sticky sessions, round-robin, retry failover, and cooldowns
operate across the provider's API keys — while **one projected OAuth grant
serves its provider**: the account whose grant is projected answers
requests directly, and one active grant per provider is kept. Per-account
ranking (rotating or load-balancing between accounts) is future work. An
account row's counters reflect that account's own successes and failures,
not a per-account traffic split. When the projected grant fails (expired
or refresh rejected), the account cools down. On a key-capable route the
pool falls back to the provider's key pool; an OAuth-only route has no
API-key pool and stops serving requests until an account is signed in
again. Recovery is a manual re-login from the account menu.

Adding an account stores only the provider-issued grant in the Harness
credential store, behind the account's `grantRef`; the manager state keeps
the reference plus non-sensitive metadata (email, account id, expiry) — the
same secret-free layout as API keys.

### Selection and failure policy

- **Sticky session**: the first request of a session selects a key and binds
  it for that session/provider pair. Later requests reuse it.
- **Round robin**: a new session advances the provider cursor and takes the
  next healthy key.
- **Retry**: a failing request is retried on the same key `retryCount` times.
- **Switch**: after the retry budget is spent, the failing key is marked
  cooling, and the session is rebound to another healthy key.
- **Cooldown**: the first failure cools a key for `baseCooldownMs`. A failure
  while cooling, or wi

plugins.description: Unofficial DeepSeek Harness plugin: answers ask_user_question with the recommended option when nobody replies in time, so an unattended session keeps working.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-plugin-auto-answer

**Unattended DSH sessions don't stall on `ask_user_question`.**

When nobody answers a question within a configurable window, this Host plugin claims
the request with the option the asker recommended — the `(Recommended)` / `（推荐）`
label — and the agent keeps working. If you *do* answer in time, your answer passes
through untouched and the plugin never intervenes.

Host-only bundle: nothing renders in the page, no browser half, no dependencies.

> **Known UI behaviour, by design — not a bug:** with a browser page attached, the question
> card stays on screen after an automatic answer until you dismiss it (「提交」/「跳过」 or a
> page reload). The answer is already recorded and the turn has continued; see
> *“The question card stays on screen after an automatic answer”* below.

## Install

```bash
# from GitHub (no build step: the source is the artifact)
dsh plugin --profile web add github:AK-blank/dsh-plugin-auto-answer

# from a local checkout while developing
dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/dsh-plugin-auto-answer
```

`dsh plugin add` writes the package into the profile and selects its bundle layer, so
the row shows up in the GUI's Plugins page and in `dsh --profile web --dump-config`
(`# == dsh-plugin-auto-answer` → `id: auto-answer`).

Installing a new bundle activates it through HMR. **Replacing an installed copy of this
plugin needs a `dsh web` restart**: Host module code is cached per process, so a changed
`lib/index.js` is not reloaded by a re-apply.

## How it works

`ask_user_question` is dispatched as the `user-questions/request` waterfall. The browser
UI answers it by rendering a question card; in a headless run nothing answers it at all.

This plugin registers **in front of** that chain (`prepend`) and calls `next()` — it is a
proxy, not a veto:

| what happens | result |
|---|---|
| a human answers inside the window | their answer wins, unchanged |
| nobody answers before the deadline | the recommended option is submitted |
| the next answerer fails outright (`NO_PROVIDER` with no page, transport ended) | the window keeps running, then the recommended option is submitted |
| the tool's own timed window expired (`ASK_TIMED_OUT`) | the recommended option is submitted immediately instead of returning `pending` |
| the turn is cancelled (`ASK_ABORTED`, signal aborted) | propagated — a cancelled turn is never answered |

The listener is registered with `{ global: true, prepend: true }`. The global flag is not
optional: Agent events are scope-filtered by the context a listener was registered on, and
a plugin installed through the plugin manager is applied inside one agent's scope — without
it the plugin would only answer the session that installed it.

## Which option counts as "recommended"

- An option label ending in `(Recommended)`, `（推荐）`, `(推荐)` or `（Recommended）`,
  case-insensitively. The option does **not** have to be first.
- The label is submitted verbatim: the marker stays in the answer, because it is the value
  the asker offered.
- Multi-select questions take every marked option.
- No marked option → `fallback` decides: `first` (default), `last`, or `none` (never answer,
  leave the question to a human).
- A question without options has nothing to choose: `freeText: skip` submits an empty
  selection — the protocol's own "skipped" answer — while `block` leaves it open.
- `plan-review` intents are **ignored by default**: approving a plan is a decision with
  consequences. `planReview: approve` / `decline` opt in explicitly.
- A batch is answered only when every question in it can be answered; the answer contract
  requires one item per question, and a partial batch would hide a human decision.

## Config

All keys are optional; the row's `config` overrides the defaults.

| key | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | master switch; `false` registers no listener at all |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `120` | window before the recommended option is chosen (5 – 86400) |
| `fallback` | `first` | `first` \| `last` \| `none` when no option is marked |
| `freeText` | `skip` | `skip` \| `block` for questions without options |
| `planReview` | `ignore` | `ignore` \| `approve` \| `decline` for plan reviews |

```yaml
# in the profile's cordis.patch.yml, after every bundle layer
- id: auto-answer
  name: 'dsh-plugin-auto-answer'
  config:
    timeoutSeconds: 90
    fallback: first
```

**With the tool's own `timed` mode**, keep `timeoutSeconds` below `tool-ask-user`'s
`timeout`; otherwise the tool returns `pending` first and this plugin's answer never
applies. The default blocking tool has no such constraint.

## Observability

Host logs in `dsh web` are not visible in the terminal, so the plugin writes an optional
JSONL trace:

```bash
DSH_AUTO_ANSWER_LOG=/tmp/auto-answer.jsonl dsh web
```

```json
{"at":"2026-10-18T03:31:56.138Z","event":"armed","agentId":"session-…","timed":false,"questions":1,"timeoutMs":20000,"picks":[{"id":"color","selected":["蓝色 (Recommended)"]}]}
{"at":"2026-10-18T03:32:16.141Z","event":"answered","agentId":"session-…","reason":"window-elapsed","timeoutMs":20000,"picks":[{"id":"color","selected":["蓝色 (Recommended)"]}]}
```

Events: `armed`, `answered`, `delegated` (a human answered), `delegate_error`, `failed`.
A broken trace path never breaks the question it describes.

## Verified behaviour

Offline self-test (`node selftest.mjs`) — 39 checks over the package contract, config
normalisation, the recommendation rules, the registration options, the timer races, and
"No unhandled rejection / no leaked timer".

Real installation path: installed into a throwaway profile with `dsh plugin add`, confirmed
as a bundle layer and row in `dsh --profile … --dump-config`, and visible on the GUI's
Plugins page under 已安装 → 无人值守自动应答.

End-to-end on a live host (blocking tool as shipped):

- **unattended**: 20 s window, question left open — the trace shows `armed` →
  `answered` exactly 20.003 s later with the recommended option, and the turn finished in
  22 s with *"你最终选择了蓝色（Recommended）。"*
- **attended**: 60 s window, the human picked the non-recommended option 24 s in — the trace
  shows `armed` → `delegated (answered-by-ui)`, the turn finished with *"你最终选了香蕉。"*,
  and the card collapsed to `1/1 已回答` normally.

## The question card stays on screen after an automatic answer — this is not a bug

**Expected behaviour, by design. Please don't file an issue for it.**

`ask_user_question` is answered through a waterfall: the browser Client renders the question
card and waits for the human's own submission, while the Host waits for whoever answers. This
plugin answers on the **Host** when the window elapses, and the Host has no message that tells
a Client its question was settled elsewhere. The card therefore stays where it was:

- it remains in the transcript, and still occupies the composer;
- the session row may keep reading 「等待回答」 (waiting for an answer).

Nothing else is affected. The `ask_user_question` result already carries the picked answer,
the turn continues and finishes normally, and the recorded session data is correct — the
stale card is browser state, not session state.

Dismiss it by clicking **提交** (submit) or **跳过** (skip), or by reloading the page.
Submitting a stale card is harmless: the request was already settled, so no late answer is
injected and no error is raised (verified). Reloading also clears the session-row label.

A Host-side plugin cannot remove that card: the card belongs to the Client's own request, and
only the Client settles it. If a future plugin should close it automatically, that needs a
Client-side change.

## Out of scope

The plugin does not touch `approval/request` (tool approvals): auto-approving a command is
a different risk class, and it is deliberately out of scope.

## Development

```bash
node selftest.mjs     # offline: no Harness, no timer left behind, no browser
```

`lib/index.js` exports `normalizeConfig`, `isRecommendedLabel`, `decideQuestion`,
`planRequest`, `createRuntime` (with injectable `now` / `setTimer` / `clearTimer` / `trace`)
and `apply` — the self-test drives the same functions the Harness loads.

MIT.

## Disclaime

plugins.description: Time-shifting task delegation for DeepSeek Harness (dsh): plan tasks at leisure, they run unattended off-peak, come back to a report. Human-adjudicated, desktop + web.
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-lowtide **Queue tasks when it's busy. They run on their own when it's cheap.** Semi-auto or full-auto, off the model's peak hours and peak prices. A must-have plugin for DeepSeek Harness. **English** | [简体中文](./README.zh-CN.md) | [繁體中文](./README.zh-HK.md) | [العربية](./docs/README.ar.md) | [Deutsch](./docs/README.de.md) | [Español](./docs/README.es.md) | [Français](./docs/README.fr.md) | [Italiano](./docs/README.it.md) | [한국어](./docs/README.ko.md)
--- ![hero](./assets/screenshots/hero.png)

Three tasks waiting in the queue, the price status glowing in the session header, auto-run when your window opens

## Introduction lowtide is a plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (dsh)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh). The problem it solves is plain and perfectly natural: Usually, when you want an agent to do some work, you sit at the computer, send the agent an instruction, wait for the reply, and then review it by hand. But this workflow seems to forget that you have plenty of idle time — and a chance to dodge the peak/off-peak pricing that some models charge. With lowtide installed, the day goes like this: whenever a job crosses your mind during the day, toss it in the queue, glance at it, release it. The tasks pile up until the time you set (say, after 7 PM — that's when DeepSeek is at valley pricing), then run by themselves. Next morning you open the report: keep what went well, send back what didn't. That's all it is. But use it for a week and your working rhythm genuinely slows down — and don't forget, "time is money, efficiency is life"... A few key capabilities: - Four execution strategies: single, iterative, sampling, review — from "one pass is enough" to "run five candidates and I'll pick" - 168 unit tests + 10 end-to-end specs, CI green across ubuntu / windows × node 22 / 24 - One build artifact serves both desktop and web — install once, works on both - Off-peak execution lands in DeepSeek's valley hours: the same batch costs about half of what peak would ## A normal day with an agent might look like this… **Ten minutes before clocking out.** You've finished reviewing code, so you file three tickets for tomorrow: a refactor (iterative, 3 rounds), a weekly report (single), and a design you're unsure about (sampling, 4 candidates). Release them all, shut down, leave. Tomorrow at your desk, the morning report says: the refactor's done, the report's drafted, and four candidate designs sit side by side, each with its cost written out. **Friday night.** Queue a week's worth of chores in one go: dependency cleanup, missing tests, data scripts. Weekends are valley price around the clock. You go out; it works from home. Monday you check the report — retry what failed, merge what's good. **A 10 AM brainwave.** You're mid-conversation with the agent about an urgent bug when you think "hey, update the docs too." The intercept card pops up: running now costs peak price, tonight it's about half — the difference is spelled out. Click "queue for off-peak"; your draft survives untouched, and you go back to the bug. **An always-on server.** You've got a machine running dsh 24/7. Switch to L3 full-auto, then file tasks from anywhere through the API (`POST /ds-lowtide/tasks`). It runs them on schedule and writes the report. Nobody's watching, but the sandbox, the daily budget, and the file locks are all still there. **Deliverables for a client.** Use the review strategy: run once, then automatically open an independent session that tears the result apart through your chosen focus (say, "hunt for data-source errors"). In the morning you don't get a bare result — you get a result plus a critical review. **Living abroad.** You're in San Francisco; DeepSeek's peak is Beijing time, which for you lands in the evening and night before. Settings converts the official hours to your local clock, one click to adopt. You set windows by your own schedule, and the books always stay aligned with the official table. ## How lowtide works ``` ① Intake ② Adjudicate ③ Execute ④ Accept Whenever you have The queue dock When the off-peak When you're back: a moment: one-click groups tasks by window opens: five open the report — from the intercept workspace; triage preflight gates pass, results + diff card, or file a → line by line: → then sandboxed runs → + actual spend ticket (4 strategies) ✓approve ⏸defer one batch per window + money saved ✕drop / approve-all ``` A task's life: `pending-review → queued → preflight → running → done / failed / stale / timeout`, plus `deferred` (postponed) and `dropped` (soft-deleted, restorable). Step two is where lowtide differs from a "fully automated script": **every task must be released by your hand before it runs** (in L2, you release the whole batch at once, 30 minutes before the window). The machine cannot move itself into the run queue. Execution is automated; decisions are not. That's why you can safely be absent. ## A tour of the lowtide interface **The new-task modal.** Four strategies side by side, each with a plain-language hint; rounds, priority, and run mode ride along per task — no trip back to settings. Tasks land as "pending review". Nothing enters the queue without passing you. ![new-task-modal](./assets/screenshots/new-task-modal.png) **Advanced options.** Model, reasoning effort, priority from 0 to 9, fresh session or continue-previous, and the locked-files list — all in one small pane. Locked files, briefly: anything on the list gets sha256-checked before execution, and if it doesn't match what you filed, the task goes stale and refuses to run. Otherwise the file you queued against could be rewritten by another task while waiting, and this one would blindly stomp on it. ![advanced-options](./assets/screenshots/advanced-options.png) **Pick any model.** Batch runs default to the official `deepseek-flash` (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the retired `deepseek-v4-flash` name still routes there at Flash prices), but each task can pick its own model — anything connected to your Harness is in the dropdown, grouped by provider. Private providers work too. Non-official models have no public price table, so the ledger honestly says "price unknown"; add a price override in settings if you want the bookkeeping exact. ![model-picker](./assets/screenshots/model-picker.png) **The window editor.** Multi-segment, overnight, per-weekday — all fine. Underneath is a live 24-hour price band: red for peak, green for valley, and a marker showing where you are right now. Outside UTC+8, one click on "adopt official peak hours" converts Beijing time to your local clock. ![window-editor](./assets/screenshots/window-editor.png) **The settings page.** Window hours, tasks per batch, per-task duration cap, concurrency, daily budget, report history, autonomy level, price overrides — all graphical, no config files. The official pricing rules (including the new all-weekend valley) are explained in human language on the same page. ![settings](./assets/screenshots/settings.png) Three more pieces of UI appear in daily use: the **price pill** (session header — busy/idle, queue size; click it to edit windows), the **peak-hours intercept card** (type at peak, it appears; the price difference is spelled out; your draft survives), and the **execution report** (the morning briefing: savings first, anomalies pinned, candidates awaiting your pick, one-click Markdown copy). ## About lowtide workspaces Every task runs inside a workspace. That single dropdown decides three things. **Which files it can touch.** Tasks run in a sandbox whose boundary is the workspace directory. Pick wrong and at best it can't find the files; at worst it edits something it shouldn't. **Who it queues with.** Tasks in the same workspace run serially (two tasks never fight over one repo); different workspaces run in paralle

plugins.description: Patch for the DSH desktop release build: liang-themed level names for dsh-thinking-slider 0.3.3 (and why Liang-Saint-Slider silently fails there)
plugins.readme_text:
# dsh-thinking-slider-liang

DSH composer 里那根思考档位滑杆，档位名换成「小难梁 / 梁子 / 梁圣 / 梁祖」。

**一条命令安装，不需要打补丁、不需要额外脚本。**

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:FkuNvidia/dsh-thinking-slider-liang
```

从系统托盘完全退出 DSH 再打开。点输入框左下角的模型名，滑杆里的档位就是中文名了。

## 效果

- 触发器：`deepseek-flash · 梁圣`
- 卡片大字档位、滑轨刻度：小难梁 / 梁子 / 梁圣 / 梁祖
- **实际发给 API 的仍是 `off / low / high / max`**，计费与能力不受影响

| 显示名 | 实际档位 |
| --- | --- |
| 小难梁 | `off` |
| 梁子 | `low` |
| 梁圣 | `high` |
| 梁祖 | `max` |

> 上游还有另一种六段映射（两个模型 × 三档：小难梁 / 牢梁 / 梁子 / 梁圣 / 梁神 / 梁祖），见 [BruzWJ/Liang-Saint-Slider](https://github.com/BruzWJ/Liang-Saint-Slider)。这里用四档版本，因为桌面端默认只挂 `deepseek-flash` 一个模型。

## 为什么不直接装上游

上游 [dsh-thinking-slider](https://github.com/MuFeng262/dsh-thinking-slider) 能用，但档位名直接照搬适配器给的 `Off / Low / High / Max`——它是刻意数据驱动的，没有改名配置。

社区里另一个更花哨的版本 [BruzWJ/Liang-Saint-Slider](https://github.com/BruzWJ/Liang-Saint-Slider) 有中文名，但**在桌面发行版上静默失效**：它的浏览器端第一行就 `require("@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives")`。这个包确实发布在 npm 上（`0.2.1-rc.2`），但没被打进桌面版的 `app.asar`。DSH 的客户端模块表是冻结的，表里没有的模块会让整个模块工厂函数抛异常，插件在浏览器里静默不注册——宿主那半照常工作（静态资源路由还能返回 200），于是表现成「装上了、没界面」。

所以这个仓库的做法是：**以上游 0.3.3 的构建产物为基础，只替换渲染层的档位名**。上游只依赖 `react` / `react-dom` / `react/jsx-runtime`，这三个内置 UI 自己也在用，所以在发行版上能跑。

## 包结构

```
package.json         dsh.bundle + dsh.client 声明
cordis.patch.yml     插入插件行
lib/index.js         Host 半（空实现）
lib/client.js        浏览器半：上游 0.3.3 产物 + 档位名映射
scripts/sync-upstream.mjs
```

`lib/client.js` 是上游构建产物（MIT）的副本，只改了一处。详见 [NOTICE](NOTICE)。

## 跟进上游

上游发新版时，不需要手工改代码：

```powershell
node scripts/sync-upstream.mjs 0.3.4
```

脚本会从 unpkg 拉取新产物、校验锚点行存在、注入映射、写出 `lib/client.js`，并打印 sha256。上游若改动了那段代码结构，脚本会直接报错而不是产出坏包——那时候改一下锚点即可（`scripts/sync-upstream.mjs` 顶部）。

改完把 `package.json` 的版本改成 `<上游版本>-liang.N`，提交推送。**从 GitHub 安装的插件不会自动更新**，重新执行一次 `dsh plugin ... add` 或先 `remove` 再 `add` 即可。

## 已验证

- DSH Desktop `0.2.1-rc.2`，Windows 11，2026-10-18
- 上游 `dsh-thinking-slider@0.3.3`
- 客户端产物 `node --check` 通过；档位切换真实写入 `reasoningEffort`

## 已知限制

- 模型列表里每行的小圆点标题（悬停 tooltip）仍走另一条代码路径，还是英文；主界面可见的档位名都已替换
- 这是构建产物副本，上游改版后需要跑一次同步脚本
- 与上游插件**不能同时装**：两者都占 `conversation.input.model` 座位，只是优先级不同，会导致行为难以预期

## 卸载

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-thinking-slider-liang
```

## 许可

MIT。上游插件与其中大部分代码归 [MuFeng262](https://github.com/MuFeng262/dsh-thinking-slider) 所有，本仓库仅做显示名替换与发行版兼容性验证。
